message.content:
One of the most celebrated sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” by Auguste Rodin** (1889).  
It was originally conceived as part of his monumental “Gates of Hell” project, but it quickly became a standalone icon. The bronze pair of lovers—intimate, sensuous, and rendered with unprecedented realism—has been endlessly reproduced, displayed in museums worldwide, and referenced in countless works of art and popular culture.  

If you’d like to know more about its history, variations, or where you can see original casts, just let me know!
